document: University of St. La Salle Graduate School Operations Manual
note: Draft for validation. Practice and Proposed rules are not confirmed by the Graduate School.

rules.rule: A student seeking admission must submit an accomplished admission application form, two letters of recommendation, one 2x2 ID picture, transcript of record, honorable dismissal or transfer credential, pass the entrance examination and interview, comply with program-specific requirements, and sign an undertaking to finish the bridging course in a year.
The entrance examination fee (Graduate School P400) and the admission fee (P300) are non-refundable.

An applicant with insufficient background must take prerequisite or bridging courses; an applicant with a non-thesis master's degree enrolls in six units of thesis as a bridging course. The number of units differs by college.

A transferee may be credited a maximum of 25% of subjects taken during the last five years that are substantially the same in content, not credited to a previous degree, upon recommendation of the Admission Committee and within the residence requirement.
A special student (audit only) needs the permission of the Dean and a signed agreement waiving the right to receive or demand credit.
A foreign student pays an additional annual foreign fee; missionaries and religious, children of Overseas Filipino workers, special exchange students and students on audit are exempt.
Upon admission the Dean gives the student information about the program of study; students who do not meet the admission test cut-off are assigned a volunteer faculty adviser.
The applicant sends a letter of intent with the transcript of records and waits for notification within 3-5 working days before taking the entrance examination.
The student number and the institutional email are created by the Registrar; the Graduate School does not generate or manually assign them.
rules.source: Consultation 15 July 2026, student number created by the Registrar; Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 3 and 4

sources.location: student number created by the Registrar

rules.rule: The admission checklist follows the official USLS admission process. The Graduate School does not repeat it; it records that admission was completed.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 4 (stakeholder-confirmed answer)

rules.rule: Student records enter the Graduate School's record through the monitoring workbook prepared from the official records (AIMS); GS staff do not create student records manually, and a missing student is checked against the official source.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 2 and 6 (stakeholder-confirmed answer); Consultation 21 July 2026, no AIMS integration

rules.rule: GS staff record the source and the date of each handoff; the Academic Coordinator confirms the program assignment; the Dean acknowledges completed onboarding.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 1

rules.rule: A possible duplicate student is identified by the student number, never by name alone; staff compare the records and confirm or merge them only when verified.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 13 and 14

rules.rule: The enrolment procedures are: (1) academic evaluation and electronic advising with the Academic Coordinator, (2) payment at the Cashiers in the Business Office, (3) validation in the student's AIMS account, (4) ID issuance or renewal.
The normal load of a part-time graduate student is six (6) to nine (9) units per semester, and twelve (12) units for a full-time student.
Attendance is counted from the first regular class meeting regardless of the time of registration.
Students with financial delinquencies at the close of the semester are not permitted to register in the succeeding semester unless previous accounts are settled.
A master's student may transfer to another master's option with the approval of the Dean, upon the recommendation of the Academic Coordinator and endorsed by the Associate Dean.

Coursework at another institution is credited only if the student secured the Dean's written permission in advance; the Registrar then issues a cross-enrollment permit. Cross-enrollment is normally allowed only to a graduating student for a course not offered in the graduating semester, and never for major elective or major professional courses.
A special class may be requested by the Academic Coordinator through the Dean, addressed to the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs. An undersized class is treated as a special class.
Enrollment takes place in AIMS. The Academic Coordinator advises the subjects and tags the student as enrolled in the Graduate School's record; the Graduate School record is a monitoring record.
There are no ordinary course-to-course prerequisites in the Graduate School; eligibility rules apply mainly to the comprehensive examination and to the thesis or dissertation stage.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 16 and 75 (stakeholder-confirmed answer)

rules.rule: Enrollment normally occurs in June to July. Dates are kept as configurable academic periods, not fixed dates.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 10 and 76 (stakeholder-confirmed answer)

rules.rule: Each student-subject pair has one status: not taken, enrolled, taken, dropped, withdrawn; and, as reported by faculty, incomplete or failed.
Faculty do not enter grades in the Graduate School record. A professor who fails a student or gives an incomplete reports it to the Academic Coordinator, who tags the status.
If the load tagged for a student is outside six to nine units (part-time) or twelve units (full-time), the platform shows a warning to the Academic Coordinator. The warning does not block the tag.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: Changing one subject for another is allowed during the first week of classes if the original subject is dissolved, if the student has a schedule conflict, or if the student fails the prerequisite subject.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: Adding subjects is allowed during the first week of classes upon the written approval of the Associate Dean.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: To add a subject: (1) un-tag the enrolment form in the Business Office, (2) secure an Advice Slip from the Graduate School Office, (3) go through the enrolment procedure.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: An undersized class is treated as a special class; the Graduate School Dean ensures that each new batch reaches the minimum number of enrollees to allow for attrition.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: A full refund is made to students for any courses discontinued by the school.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: Course adjustments (change and add) may continue until the first week of classes.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 10, 34 and 77 (stakeholder-confirmed answer)

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: The Academic Coordinator chooses the subjects to offer by studying which subjects students have and have not taken; each offering states the subject, the schedule and the professor; the Academic Coordinator decides who teaches it.

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: A subject counts as needed when at least one student needs it. A need is not an offering: subject need, proposed offering, approved offering and scheduled class are kept separate.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 31 and 85 (answer attributed to the Associate Dean); Consultation 29 July 2026, the group reports the demand cutoff of one as the Associate Dean's answer

sources.location: July 20 checklist, items 31 and 85 (answer attributed to the Associate Dean)
the group reports the demand cutoff of one as the Associate Dean's answer

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: Offerings are planned during the term break, after the previous semester ends and before enrollment.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 34; Consultation 29 July 2026 rehearsal

sources.location: July 20 checklist, item 34; Consultation 29 July 2026 rehearsal

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: The Dean approves the offering plan before it is published.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 3

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: When the Academic Coordinator decides not to offer a subject, the platform shows which students would be delayed, so that the decision can be made with that information; the decision stays with the Academic Coordinator.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 32, 33 and 86

rules.process: Course offering and course adjustments (change and add of subject)
rules.rule: When assigning a professor the Academic Coordinator considers the professor's preferred subjects, availability, qualifications, current load and schedule conflicts; the platform only suggests.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 36-40, 88-90

rules.rule: The student may withdraw subjects until the second week from the start of classes regardless of whether or not classes have been attended.

Ten percent (10%) of the total amount due for the term is charged if the withdrawal is within the first week of classes, and twenty percent (20%) if within the second week, regardless of whether or not classes have been attended.
The student retains the right to withdraw all subjects at any time of the semester after the second week but pays the full enrolment fees for the semester.

The student may be charged all school fees in full if withdrawal is made at any time after the second week of classes. If the withdrawal is due to a justifiable reason, the student is charged pertinent fees only up to and including the last month of attendance.
A student may seek a refund if he or she withdraws during the first two weeks of classes when tuition and other fees have been paid in full, or for any length longer than one month.
To file a withdrawal of subject, the student writes a letter and seeks approval from the Dean.
Once approved, the student accomplishes the Withdrawal Form and settles all financial obligations.
The accomplished Withdrawal Form is provided to the Registrar, the Accounting Office, and the student.
The grade symbol W means Withdrawn.

A subject withdrawal (from one subject, not from the Graduate School) before or in the first week of classes does not count against the student; dropping is the act of leaving a subject in the middle of the semester.

An approved withdrawal is sent to the Registrar, which processes it in the registration system, and then to the Business Office for any fee arrangement. The Graduate School's responsibility ends at sending the request to the Registrar.
After the Registrar has been sent the request, the Graduate School tags the subject as withdrawn (a manual tag is enough), with the date applied, the date granted and a text area for the result.

According to the Associate Dean, a student may withdraw before classes begin or in the first week of classes; the Dean decides with discretion, and a request submitted after the deadline or with an insufficient or inconsistent justification is normally denied. (This is a second-hand account recorded by the group and conflicts with the Handbook's second week; see OQ-01.)
rules.source: Consultation 29 July 2026, account of the Associate Dean's answer

sources.location: account of the Associate Dean's answer

rules.rule: The platform shows the student the Handbook's fee bracket for the date of the request (first week, second week, later) as information only; the Business Office computes the fee.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: Students are expected to attend classes regularly; the maximum number of absences allowed a student is 20% of the total number of class hours for the whole semester.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A student may be excused for a death in the family, illness (with a medical certificate from the USLS clinic or a personal doctor), or a graduate program activity endorsed by the Dean. Excuses are for time missed only, and all work missed must be made up to the satisfaction of the professor within a reasonable time.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: When unexcused absence reaches more than 20% of the stipulated hours in one course, the student is automatically dropped from the course by the professor and is given a grade of DRP with a 5.0 grade.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A student who takes part in a school-sponsored activity or represents the University in an official capacity is granted an Approved Absence on the Dean's approval; it is not counted against the allowed absences.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: The grade symbols D (Dropped) and W (Withdrawn) appear in the grading system; students with grades INC, D or W, or who repeated a subject, are not eligible for the special academic honors.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: If a student gets a 5.0 he or she is automatically dropped from the program; failure in any subject means no re-admission to the program.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A student drops a subject during the semester by talking or writing to the Academic Coordinator. Once agreed, the Academic Coordinator or GS staff tag the subject as dropped with a date and notes. No student-facing drop request is needed in the Graduate School's record.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: The Graduate School drops the subject in AIMS as well as in its own record.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A drop requested by a student is recorded without a Graduate School approval step (there is no Deny). The status moves from requested to recorded and stays marked as awaiting confirmation until the Graduate School has seen the change in AIMS.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, items 18, 19 and 79 (revision adopted after the 15 July adviser session)

sources.location: July 20 checklist, items 18, 19 and 79 (revision adopted after the 15 July adviser session)

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A request made up to the end of the second week of classes is handled as a withdrawal (see WD-01); a request made later is recorded as a drop. The Handbook does not give this dividing line; it is the group's reading of the Associate Dean's distinction between withdrawal and dropping.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: To remain in good standing a master's student must maintain a weighted average of 2.0 or better, and a doctorate student 1.75 or better, at the end of each academic year; a grade of 3.0 (master's) or 2.0 (doctorate) is passing but carries no graduate credit.

rules.process: Dropping, including being dropped for absences
rules.rule: A grade of INC may be given if the class standing is passing but the student fails to take the final examination or complete other requirements for illness or other valid reasons. It is removed within one academic year by meeting all course requirements and submitting the Incomplete Grade Removal Form to the Graduate School Office within the set deadline; after a year without compliance the grade becomes 3.0 (master's) or 2.0 (doctorate) and the subject is taken again; a student with INC in all subjects is dropped from the rolls of the Graduate School.
A student who does not intend to enroll in a semester may apply for a leave of absence; a student on leave does not sever his or her ties with the University.
A request for a leave of absence is made in writing to the Dean and states the reason for the leave and specifies the period.
The leave may be approved for a period of one (1) year but may be renewed for at most another year.
LOA must be done on or before the deadline.
A student who does not intend to enroll for a valid reason (medical reasons) but still has remaining units to enroll is not allowed to enroll in Residency but should file for a Leave of Absence.
A student may file an LOA if the student withdraws after two weeks of classes have elapsed; the student is subject to a withdrawal fee from the Cashier's office.
The Dean, Associate Dean, or the duly authorized representative informs the University Registrar of the leave, indicating the reasons and the amount of money refunded to the student, if any.
For a leave availed of by the student during the second half of the semester, the class standing of the courses enrolled is W (withdrawn); no refund of tuition and fees is provided.
No leave of absence is granted during the semester within two (2) weeks before the last day of classes.
A master's program must be finished within seven academic years and a doctoral program within nine academic years, including the leave of absence.
A student who withdraws from the college without a formal leave of absence is considered absent without leave (AWOL) and has registration privileges curtailed or entirely withdrawn.
The student may file the leave through a structured form in place of a letter, provided the Dean accepts the form as the written request.
rules.source: Group working notes, Consultation 20 July 2026 rehearsal (structured form suggested by the adviser)

sources.location: Consultation 20 July 2026 rehearsal (structured form suggested by the adviser)

rules.rule: The platform checks a leave request for an approved reason category, a valid start and end term, the student's earlier approved leaves and a future start term, and gives the Dean a recommendation; the Dean decides.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): LOA policy review

rules.process: Return from leave of absence and readmission
rules.rule: A student returning from a leave of absence (LOA) or absence without leave (AWOL) declares his or her intention to enroll by writing to the University Registrar through the Graduate School Dean, who then endorses it to the University Registrar.

rules.process: Return from leave of absence and readmission
rules.rule: A returnee must present: (1) clearance from the Business Office, (2) an interview (reason for delay, residency requirements), (3) evaluation of subject and grade requirements, (4) an Advise Slip from the Dean.

rules.process: Return from leave of absence and readmission
rules.rule: Failure in any subject means no re-admission to the program.

rules.process: Return from leave of absence and readmission
rules.rule: A student who cannot finish within the maximum residence (seven years for a master's, nine for a doctorate) must re-enroll all courses taken and earn new credits.

rules.process: Return from leave of absence and readmission
rules.rule: The platform's readmission checklist asks for a structured return intention, a confirmed updated study plan, a program or adviser consultation, and confirmation that no accountability is pending. The Handbook's four requirements (RDM-02) are the official list.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): readmission requirements

rules.rule: A student who withdraws from a college without a formal leave of absence is considered in "absent without leave" status (AWOL) and has registration privileges curtailed or entirely withdrawn.
A student returning from AWOL declares the intention to enroll by writing to the University Registrar through the Graduate School Dean, who endorses it to the Registrar.
A returnee presents a Business Office clearance, an interview, an evaluation of subject and grade requirements and an Advise Slip from the Dean.
An AWOL status has the same effect as a leave of absence for reporting: it is communicated to the Registrar.
rules.source: Consultation 20 July 2026, adviser's statement; not confirmed by Graduate School staff

sources.location: adviser's statement; not confirmed by Graduate School staff

rules.rule: AWOL is flagged from source evidence (an imported AWOL standing, or a full semester without enrollment and without an approved leave), not typed in by a user.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): AWOL policy review

rules.rule: On return, the student is classified by years in the program: within the normal limit (five years master's, seven years doctorate), extension with a graded six-unit refresher (up to seven and nine), or full re-enrollment beyond that.

Students who have finished all their coursework and are just working on their thesis or dissertation and practicum or internship, after a semester of enrollment for thesis writing and practicum, may enroll for residence.

Students who are not enrolled in any subject but who want to complete an INC, will take the comprehensive exam, or are waiting for their research publication must also enroll for residence. Registration for residence should be done within the semester.
A student who does not intend to enroll for a valid reason but still has remaining units is not allowed to enroll in Residency, but files a leave of absence.
For the comprehensive examination the Academic Coordinator does the initial evaluation and the student is advised to enroll in Residency in Comprehensive Examination.
Master's program: candidacy must be attained within three academic years from the date of admission and all requirements completed within five academic years.
Master's program: a student who cannot comply within five years is allowed a maximum two-year extension but must enroll in a graded six-unit refresher course related to the area of specialization.

A master's program must be finished within a maximum of seven academic years including leave of absence; a student who cannot finish within seven years must re-enroll all the courses taken and earn new credits.
Doctorate program: candidacy within five academic years from admission; all requirements including the dissertation within seven academic years.

Doctorate program: beyond seven years a maximum two-year extension with a graded six-unit refresher course; the program must be finished within nine academic years including leave of absence, after which the student must re-enroll all courses taken and earn credit units.
Thesis or project paper writing must be finished within two years from the title or proposal defense; dissertation writing within three years from the title defense.

The platform records each residency enrollment with its purpose (thesis or dissertation work, practicum or internship, comprehensive examination, awaiting publication) and marks a purpose as unsupported if the student's record does not match it.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): residency policy review

rules.rule: The comprehensive examinations cover all basic or core courses, fields of concentration, and electives or cognates. They are given for two days for a master's and three days for a doctorate, with two-day intervals between examinations or consecutively as arranged, and last a maximum of eight hours per day.
Master's scope: first day basic courses and electives or cognates; second day major courses. Doctorate scope: first day basic courses and electives or cognates; second and third days major courses.

Master's students who have passed all academic requirements and been evaluated by their Graduate School Academic Coordinators may file an application; doctorate students evaluated by their College Deans may likewise file.

Non-thesis students must have completed the integrating courses (feasibility study, project study, case study or applied research in the major field for MBA; action research or practicum in the major field for Education).

The application is filed with the Graduate Program Secretary at least two weeks before the scheduled examination; an examinee who withdraws the application informs the Graduate Program in writing with the reason at least three working days before the examination.
The examination fee is P1,100 for a master's and P2,500 for a doctorate, paid to the Business Office; the official receipt attached to the application is presented to the secretary before the exam.
The fee is forfeited if the examinee fails to appear during the examination dates or fails to inform the Graduate Program Services Office by a written note.

A student must get a minimum score of 7.00 points (70%) in all courses to pass. A student below 7.00 may take a first retake in the failed courses within the residency enrollment and is allowed two retakes within the semester.

A student who fails the second retake takes a refresher course on the failed courses the following semester and may take the examination for the third and last time in the following residency enrollment; failure the fourth time means disqualification from the program.
A student who passes the comprehensive examination confers with the Dean for a thesis or dissertation adviser and is considered advanced to candidacy.
Passing the comprehensive examination is a graduation requirement; for special academic honors the examination must be passed with no retake.
The monitoring workbook records the comprehensive examination in its own column.
rules.source: Group working notes, Monitoring workbook, COMPRE column

rules.rule: The platform accepts a title defense application only after the comprehensive examination is passed and all curriculum subjects are complete.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): comprehensive exam eligibility

rules.rule: The application for title defense (Form 1 and three concept papers to the Academic Coordinator) must be made at least two weeks before the scheduled defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 59; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part I, step 2 note

sources.location: Title Defense, Part I, step 2 note

rules.rule: The Research Coordinator nominates the panel members as recommended by the Academic Coordinator, after deliberation with the GS Research Committee.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 60; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part I, step 4

rules.rule: Panel for a project paper: one panel chair and two members (one content specialist and one method specialist). Thesis or bridging thesis: one chair and three members (one content specialist, one method specialist and one external panel). Dissertation: one chair and four members (two content specialists, one method specialist and one external panel). The chair and the content and method specialists are University-affiliated; the external panel is a content or industry expert who takes part from the proposal defense onwards.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 60; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part I, step 4

rules.rule: The panel members deliberate the three submitted titles without the presence of the student; the chair then admits the student.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 60; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part II

rules.rule: The panel chair may record the defense with the consent of everyone in the meeting room and furnish the student the link of the recording.
The panel chair emails the accomplished Form 2 to the Research Coordinator and the student within the first working day after the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 61; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part III, step 2

rules.rule: If the proposed titles are disapproved, the student presents a new set of three titles and follows the same protocol; the decision is reflected in Form 2.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 61; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part III, step 3

rules.rule: The student asks the panel about their preferred mode of payment, settles the title defense fees and emails the proof to the GS mailbox within the first working day after the defense, with the subject line LAST NAME_type of defense_receipt.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 61; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part III, step 4

rules.rule: Thesis or project paper writing must be finished within two years from the title or proposal defense; for the thesis the student has one year from the title defense to submit and defend a proposal. Dissertation writing must be finished within three years from the title defense, with one year to submit and defend a proposal.
If the approved title is still applicable, the same concept paper may be presented for re-defense; otherwise the student changes the research title or topic and goes through the title defense again.
GS staff check that Form 1, three concept papers and the Academic Coordinator's endorsement are present before the Research Coordinator nominates a panel. The check is for completeness only.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 42; Group working notes, transactions list

sources.location: July 20 checklist, item 42; Group working notes, transactions list

rules.rule: The platform does not schedule a title defense, nominate a panel or approve a title by itself; panel candidates are suggested from faculty specialization, availability and workload and staff may choose any faculty.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 44

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The research adviser must be affiliated with the University and the degree program must be aligned with the student's program.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 61; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, step 1

sources.location: Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, step 1

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Protocol: the research adviser must have a PhD degree for PhD students and at least PhD units for MA students (CHED CMO 15), and should have a maximum of five active advisees for the current academic year.
rules.source: Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, step 1 note

sources.location: Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, step 1 note

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Handbook: the adviser shall be a faculty of the Graduate School and a holder of a doctoral degree aligned with the discipline, with at least one publication in a refereed journal or publicly recognized creative or technology outputs (CMO 15 s. 2019).

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: In the exigency of service a faculty member may have more than five advisees with the approval of the Dean.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The student may express a preference, but the Dean, the Associate Dean and the Research Coordinator make the final decision based on the degree, expertise, research work, number of advisees (maximum five per semester) and total workload of the faculty member.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The choice of adviser gives primary importance to the student's choice with the approval of the program adviser and the Dean; the Dean appoints the adviser on the basis of expertise in the student's topic following the Research Protocol.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Faculty of other universities may serve as adviser in some circumstances if they are adjunct faculty of the Graduate School.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The assignment of an adviser may be done while the student is still taking academic courses.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Form 3 is emailed by the student to the Academic Coordinator, who notes it to the Research Coordinator; the Dean's e-signature is not required at that point; the Research Coordinator emails Form 3 to the Dean; the Research Coordinator, the Associate Dean and the Dean sign; the Research Coordinator emails Form 3.1 to the student and adviser, who email the accomplished form back.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 61; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, steps 2-5

sources.location: Designation of the Research Adviser, Part I, steps 2-5

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The advisee and adviser accomplish Form 3.2 and Form 3.3; the student emails them to the Research Coordinator within five days of receipt of Form 3.1.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 61-62; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Designation of the Research Adviser, Part II

sources.location: Designation of the Research Adviser, Part II

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The adviser is bound only to advising and shall not be selected as editor of the student or to any other appointment related to the conduct of the study.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The adviser monitors the research according to the timetable in Form 3.2, reviews submitted proposals, questionnaires and chapters, gives technical and moral guidance, conducts a mock defense when necessary, attends the defense of the advisee, attends orientations set by the Graduate School, and adheres to the Research Protocol.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: A student may make only one request to change the title of the study, before the proposal defense application: Form 3.4 and the new concept paper go to the adviser, who endorses the request to the panel; the panel deliberates and the chair emails the decision.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 62; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Change of Title of the Study

sources.location: Change of Title of the Study

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: A student may make only one request to change the research adviser, before the proposal defense, for justifiable reasons: Form 3.1.1 signed by the current and new adviser, deliberated by the Research Coordinator, Associate Dean and Dean; then a new Form 3.1.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 62; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Request for Change of Research Adviser

sources.location: Request for Change of Research Adviser

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: An adviser designated before the effectivity of his or her retirement may continue to serve until the final defense.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: The student needs to propose three faculty as adviser options.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Each nominated faculty member may accept or decline the nomination in the platform (the Associate Dean suggested this); the student and the Graduate School then choose among those who accept.

rules.process: Adviser designation, advising contract, change of title and change of adviser
rules.rule: Adviser-dependent steps (adviser signature, endorsement, document review, availability in scheduling) are blocked until an adviser is designated.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 43

rules.rule: Before the proposal defense the student must have consulted a statistician for a quantitative study, with Form 4.1 accomplished by the statistician. Form 4.1 is not required for qualitative studies.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 63; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (statistical consultation)

rules.rule: The research adviser accomplishes Form 4 with e-signature once the paper complies with the research paper guidelines set by the Graduate School Office; this must be done at least two weeks before the date of the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 63; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (Form 4 endorsement and note)

sources.location: Proposal Defense, Part I (Form 4 endorsement and note)

rules.rule: The panel members are given two weeks to review the paper before the scheduled proposal defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 63; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (panel review period)

sources.location: Proposal Defense, Part I (panel review period)

rules.rule: The adviser's recommendation of an external panel is subject to the approval of the GS Research Committee (Dean, Associate Dean, Academic Coordinator, Research Coordinator) according to the Protocol, and to the approval of the GS office according to the Handbook.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 63; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (external panel recommendation)

sources.location: Proposal Defense, Part I (external panel recommendation)

rules.rule: For co-authorship, the student must have the major part and contribute at least 80% during the conduct of the study and must adhere to the contribution of work in Form 4.2; co-authorship or study grant agreements follow the institutional guidelines of the Center for Research and Engagement.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 64; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part II (co-authorship note)

rules.rule: The panel deliberates the paper first without the student and the adviser; if major revisions are recommended the student is advised to do a re-defense following the same protocol, reflected in Form 5.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 64; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part II

rules.rule: The panel chair emails the consolidated Form 5 to the student, the adviser and the Research Coordinator within the first working day after the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 64; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part III (consolidated Form 5)

rules.rule: The application for ethics review (Form 5.2 with the revised manuscript and Form 5.1) is made within one month after the proposal defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part III (ethics review note)

sources.location: Proposal Defense, Part III (ethics review note)

rules.rule: The student settles payment to the preferred method of the panel members and emails the proof to the GS mailbox within the first working day after the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part III (payment)

rules.rule: A student who has used a change of title or a change of adviser must have done so before the proposal defense application (ADV-13, ADV-14).
Ethics clearance is needed before the closed-door final defense: the adviser emails Form 4, the Ethics Clearance and the manuscript to the Research Coordinator.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (Form 4 submission)

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (Form 4 submission)

rules.rule: The Research Coordinator records ethics clearance as received; the office checks that the document is present, not its content.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 42

rules.rule: The platform blocks the proposal endorsement without an adviser, and, for quantitative studies, without Form 4.1.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 43; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: Final decisions are pass, pass with minor revisions, and provisional pass with major revisions (subject for re-defense).
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 66; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part II

rules.rule: The adviser emails Form 4, the Ethics Clearance and the manuscript to the Research Coordinator at least two weeks before the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (Form 4 submission)

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (Form 4 submission)

rules.rule: 14-Day Rule: "At least fourteen (14) days, inclusive of weekends, from the date the panel members of the oral defense received their copies of the thesis/dissertation to the date of the oral defense."
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 66; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

rules.rule: The same set of panel members takes part in the closed-door final defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 66; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (same panel)

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I (same panel)

rules.rule: The panel members must not agree with the proposed schedule without the revised manuscript; the manuscript must already have been given to the panel before the date is set.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

rules.rule: If a provisional pass with major revisions is given and the panel recommends a re-defense, the student follows the same protocol for the final defense afterward; the same amount of fees applies to the re-defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part II note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part II note

rules.rule: If a provisional pass with major revisions is given but no re-defense is recommended, the student complies with the corrections; once the revised manuscript is given to the panel for approval the 14-Day Rule applies; the adviser accomplishes Form 8 and emails it to the GS Research Coordinator.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part II

rules.rule: A student who fails to meet the recommendations of all the panel members at a given time is advised to re-defend following the same protocol.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part II

rules.rule: A provisional pass with major revisions must be reflected in Form 6 and agree with the score in Form 7: for a thesis the score is below 85; for a dissertation the score is below 90.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part II note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part II note

rules.rule: Each panel member accomplishes Form 6 and emails it to the panel chair, and accomplishes Form 7 and emails it to the Research Coordinator, within the first working day after the defense (the Protocol adds that the research adviser also accomplishes Form 7); the chair emails all Forms 6 and the consolidated comments to the Research Coordinator, adviser and student within the same time.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III

rules.rule: For students admitted on August 2020 and onwards, the student is given two to four weeks to prepare and apply for the public final defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 71; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part IV

rules.rule: Form 4.3 must be fully accomplished with the e-signature of the panel members and the date the panel received the revised manuscript.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 72-73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part I (Form 4.3 notes)

rules.rule: Form 6 must state the Action Taken by the student to address each comment and the specific page number where the improvement appears.

Application for the public final defense must be made 5 days before the preferred schedule for posting purposes; Form 4.3 must be submitted at least two weeks before the date of the defense. (The two periods conflict; see OQ-23.)
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 72-73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part I (Form 4.3 notes)

rules.rule: The announcement of the public defense is posted on the Graduate School Official Facebook Page with an embedded pre-registration link; the Research Coordinator coordinates campus entry with the GS Office.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part I (announcement and pre-registration)

sources.location: Public Defense, Part I (announcement and pre-registration)

rules.rule: Students enrolled (admitted) before August 2020 are not required to do a public final defense; instead, after the closed-door final defense, the student presents at a research conference.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 68-69; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part III note

rules.rule: In the public final defense the student has 30 minutes to present; the Handbook adds another 30 minutes for questions and answers, and the audience may ask questions. Panel members must have Form 6 in hand to check compliance.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part II

rules.rule: Only the panel chair submits the defense verdict and the record of the result.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 48

rules.rule: After the student revises the paper, the manuscript is emailed to the panel members for their approval before Turnitin scanning and editing; the 14-Day Rule is applied, and the panel members then email the student confirming their initial approval.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 68; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III-IV

rules.rule: The adviser verifies that the panelists' recommendations are reflected in the manuscript and then endorses it for Turnitin scanning and editing.
rules.source: Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III (adviser verification)

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part III (adviser verification)

rules.rule: The final draft undergoes Turnitin scanning; a similarity index rating (SIR) of not more than 15% is required before the paper goes to the editor.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 68; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III

rules.rule: The student chooses from the pool of editors affiliated with the University so that the USLS IRF is employed; the 14-Day Rule applies to the editor; the editor gives Form 9, Editor Certification, once corrections are carried out.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 68; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III

rules.rule: The student sends the soft copy of the final manuscript to the GS Office, copy furnished to the research ethics office, with the panel approval emails, ethics clearance, Turnitin certificate and editor's certification, within the period set by the office, to inform the office that the manuscript is ready for hard-bound reproduction.
The GS Office coordinates with the panel members and advisers for the accomplishment of Form 10, Approval Sheet.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 68; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III

rules.rule: The student submits the bound copies and CD with the signed approval sheets as part of the requirements for the diploma, TOR and other related documents.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 68; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part III

rules.rule: The student presents the thesis or dissertation at a research conference (the Graduate School Research Conference or an external one); the certificate of presentation for an external conference may be submitted after the bound copies and CD. Only graduating students present at the Graduate School Research Conference and join the graduation ceremony.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 68-69, 74; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part III note

rules.rule: Publication: the student chooses a journal from the list of the Publication and Engagement Office and accomplishes Form 12 (Scopus, ISI and Web of Science for PhD; peer-reviewed journals for MA students); the manuscript, ethics clearance (if applicable), Form 11 (if applicable) and Form 12 go to the GS Research Coordinator for review by the Research Committee (Research Coordinator, Academic Coordinator, Associate Dean and the external expert); the Dean approves; the student then files Form 13 with the copy of the journal or the certificate of publication.
The student can only be declared a graduate and join the graduation ceremony once Form 13 and a copy of the journal or certificate of publication has been submitted.
The published journal must include the authorship affiliation in the sample format given in the Handbook.
The best thesis or dissertation award requires a cut-off score of 96 points; the chairman of the committee or the Dean submits the work to the committee and approval by the majority is required.
The office checks that each completion document is present and that the Turnitin certificate shows a rating of 15% or below; it does not verify the content of the documents.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 42; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: For the title defense the GS Office coordinates with the panel members about the proposed schedule; the Research Coordinator informs the panel and the student of the date and time.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, p. 60; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Title Defense, Part I, steps 5-6

rules.rule: For the proposal and final defenses the student and the research adviser agree with the panel members on the date and time, and the agreed schedule is indicated in Form 4.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 63, 65; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (agreed schedule)

rules.rule: Lead times: title defense application at least two weeks before the defense; Form 4 at least two weeks before the proposal or final defense; the panel has two weeks to review the manuscript; under the 14-Day Rule at least fourteen days, inclusive of weekends, pass from the date the panel receives the manuscript to the defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 59, 63, 65-66; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

sources.location: Closed-door Final Defense, Part I note

rules.rule: Public final defense: Form 4.3 must be submitted five days before the preferred schedule for posting purposes (and at least two weeks before the defense according to the same section; OQ-23).
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 72-73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Public Defense, Part I (Form 4.3 notes)

rules.rule: The panel chair coordinates with the GS Office for the venue (proposal and closed-door final defense); the GS Office reserves the venue for the public final defense. For students abroad the defense is online.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 63, 66, 70, 73; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part I (venue and students abroad)

sources.location: Proposal Defense, Part I (venue and students abroad)

rules.rule: The panel members must not agree with a proposed schedule without the revised manuscript.
A re-defense follows the same protocol as the original defense.
rules.source: Handbook 2022-2023, pp. 64, 66-67; Research Protocol AY2024-2025, Proposal Defense, Part II (major revisions)

rules.rule: Faculty invited to a panel may accept the invitation for the proposed date or mark themselves unavailable (the Associate Dean suggested this).
rules.source: Consultation 21 July 2026, Associate Dean's suggestion for panel scheduling

sources.location: Associate Dean's suggestion for panel scheduling

rules.rule: A defense is confirmed only when all required panel members and the adviser are available on the date and the lead time has passed; the student may ask for a schedule revision with new preferred dates; the reason for a reschedule is recorded.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 9; Platform (current build)

sources.location: BPM accurate flow, section 9; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: Students who have finished all their coursework and are just working on the practicum or internship, after a semester of enrollment for it, may enroll for residence.
For the non-thesis track in Education, the integrating course (action research or practicum in the major field) must be completed before the student files for the comprehensive examination.

The curriculum copied in the group's notes for the Doctor of Philosophy in Psychology lists DPSY330 Internship (six units) in the second semester of the second year, before the written comprehensive examination and the dissertation. (The document the curriculum was copied from is not identified in the notes.)
rules.source: Group working notes, 'Course stuff' section, program curriculum tables

rules.rule: The practicum workflow applies only to students in Psychology programs and in the Master of Science in Guidance and Counseling (MSGC); students of other programs are excluded.
rules.source: Group working notes, Proposal and scenario notes, practicum program restriction; Platform (current build)

sources.location: Proposal and scenario notes, practicum program restriction; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: A student may begin the practicum only after the platform's check of curriculum completion and research progress is satisfied; if source data are missing the check shows Needs verification, not Pass.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build): practicum eligibility

rules.rule: The student submits a signed MOA, the practicum site and the supervisor's name; GS staff record and forward it; the Academic Coordinator reviews it and marks the practicum as in progress.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 11

rules.rule: The required practicum hours default to 200; the practicum cannot be marked completed below the required hours; completion evidence is one or more certificate PDFs, and several certificates are allowed when the hours come from different companies.
rules.source: Group working notes, Platform (current build); proposal notes

rules.rule: If the hours are short, the Academic Coordinator returns the case with a reason; the student submits additional evidence; the earlier files stay in the history and are not overwritten.
rules.source: Group working notes, Scenario notes, practicum unusual case

rules.rule: The Academic Coordinator verifies hours and documents and sends a completed status report to the Dean; the Dean reviews the report and marks it reviewed. The Dean does not approve or deny the practicum.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 11

rules.rule: A student will only be considered a graduate of the University after completing all the requirements listed below; a student will not be allowed to go up the stage if requirements are not met.
The student must be officially enrolled during the semester of application for graduation.
The student must have completed all the prescribed subjects for the degree.
The student must have passed the comprehensive examination.
The student must have completed a successful final oral defense of the project paper, thesis or dissertation, and complied with the required revisions.

The student must submit one bound approved copy of the project paper, thesis or dissertation and one CD. The bound copy conforms to the standard format of the University and contains the official approval by the members of the defense panel and the official acceptance by the Dean.
The student must have paid all financial obligations to the University; the Graduate School may withhold reports of grades, transcripts of records and diplomas of students who have not fully paid.
The student must have presented the thesis or dissertation in a public seminar series.
The student must have published at least one research paper while enrolled in the program in a Scopus-indexed, Web of Science and ISI journal, for those enrolled from AY 2022-2023 onwards.
Graduating students are required to attend the Alumni seminar given by the Alumni Director.
The Office of the Registrar certifies the eligibility of candidates for graduation and honors.

Academic honors: Highest Academic Honor needs a GPA of 1.1 or better and no grade lower than 1.25; High Academic Honor needs a GPA of 1.25 or better and no grade lower than 1.25 (doctoral) or 1.5 (master's). Both need moral and academic integrity, no repeated subject, no INC, D or W grade, and passing the comprehensive examination with no re-take.

GS staff compile the candidate list; the Academic Coordinator checks coursework; the Research Coordinator validates the research completion documents; GS staff prepare the endorsement list; the Dean approves it and sends it to the Registrar.
rules.source: Group working notes, BPM accurate flow, section 12

rules.rule: A student is eligible for selection into a graduation batch only after coursework, research and practicum (where applicable) are complete and the student has submitted a signed graduation application; an application with incorrect information is returned and replaced by a completely new corrected document, the original being kept.
rules.source: Group working notes, Scenario notes, graduation standard and unusual cases; Platform (current build)

sources.location: Scenario notes, graduation standard and unusual cases; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: Candidates are reviewed within a graduation review window for a school year opened and closed by the Graduate School; the dates, the treatment of late applicants and the treatment of eligible students who miss the window are to be set by the Graduate School.
rules.source: Group working notes, Scenario notes; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: After the Dean approves a batch, the endorsed list is exported as a file and the Dean sends it to the Registrar by the official email; the platform records the export and the status Exported — Ready to Send, and does not record that an email was sent or that the Registrar acknowledged it.
rules.source: Group working notes, Scenario notes; Platform (current build)

rules.rule: The accomplished Withdrawal Form is provided to the Registrar, the Accounting Office, and the student.
The Dean, Associate Dean or authorized representative informs the University Registrar of a leave of absence, indicating the reasons and the amount of money refunded to the student, if any.
The Graduate School Dean endorses a returning student's written intention to enroll to the University Registrar.

Cross-enrollment: the Dean's written permission is presented to the Registrar, who issues the cross-enrollment permit; after the course the student submits the grade to the Registrar for inclusion in the academic record.

A professor submits his or her grades within one year after the course was enrolled; an error in grades is corrected after the professor explains in writing to the Dean and secures approval, before the Registrar submits grades to CHED.
The Registrar is the repository of the records of academic performance and certifies the eligibility of candidates for graduation and honors.

For a withdrawal, the request is sent to the Registrar, who processes it in the system, and the Business Office then arranges any tuition adjustment; the Graduate School's responsibility ends at sending the request to the Registrar.
There is no integration between AIMS and the Graduate School record. The Graduate School cannot pull data from AIMS and may ask the ITS for an Excel export.

The Graduate School keeps a log of each handoff (what, when, by whom, to which office) and of the Registrar's confirmation when one is received; the platform does not claim that the Registrar has acted until a confirmation is recorded.
rules.source: Group working notes, July 20 checklist, item 57; Consultation 20 July 2026, adviser's remark that the Registrar must confirm

sources.location: adviser's remark that the Registrar must confirm

rules.rule: The export for the Registrar is a file (for withdrawals, an Excel list of approved withdrawals; for graduation, a CSV list of endorsed candidates) sent by the responsible person by email; column layouts are to be confirmed by the Registrar.
rules.source: Group working notes, Scenario notes; Platform (current build)
